correctness.rationale: If F²(x,w)=(x,w), the accumulator balance forces x1=-x; nontrivial points have x=u>0, and both first-coordinate equations require cosθ=cos(θ+ku)=C/u² with C=1+1/a. The trigonometric zero factor yields exhaustive A (ku=2πm, two phases) and B (θ=-ku/2+jπ, |cos(ku/2)|=C/u²) branches, intersecting only at u=√C=2πm/k. Near each distant z_n=(2n+1)π/k, monotonicity of |cos(ku/2)| against C/u² yields exactly two B roots with u=z_n±2C/(k z_n²)+O(z_n^-5), giving N_2(R)=2kR/π+O(1). Explicit one-step Jacobian with d=-2a-3, b=aku³ sinθ leads to A return J_-J_+ of det d²-b²<0 and B return J_+² of det (d-b)²>0; both eigenvalue moduli are asymptotic aku³ and hyperbolically repelling beyond finite cutoffs. For 0<a<1, |x|<√(a^-1-1) contracts by a(1+x0²)<1, w converges, radius is sharp for uniform phase-wise contraction. Independently bisected distant B roots and computed return spectra in four cases; this corroborates, not replaces, the asymptotic proof.
